newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's YUKOS oil issues stock to help pay debts.
newsitem.headline: Russia's YUKOS oil issues stock to help pay debts.

text.p: Shareholders of Russia's NK YUKOS oil company, parent of Yuganskneftegaz, approved a 35 percent capital increase to help pay off debts at an extraordinary meeting on Saturday, Russian news agencies said.
They said the new issue of 580 million shares would have a nominal value of four roubles each, taking the company's nominal capital to 8.9 billion roubles from the current 6.6 billion roubles.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted YUKOS president Sergei Muravlenko as saying that the 527 billion roubles profit from the emission would cover wage arrears of around 350 billion roubles.
The remainder would go towards paying off 1.9 trillion roubles of debts to the federal government, it said, adding that Muravlenko said the company planned further issues next year.
AOOT NK YUKOS is one of around a dozen vertically integrated oil companies set up in recent years. Its Yuganskneftegaz unit is Russia's second-largest oil producer.
In a December 1995 shares-for-loans auction of government assets, Russia's Bank Menatep won a 33 percent stake in YUKOS and the right to manage an additional 45 percent. ($1 = 5,376 roubles)
